researchAudit.evidenceExcerpt:
## Why the West Rules—for Now: The Patterns of History, and What They Reveal About the Future

Ian Morris · 2010 · 77/100 · Below target. Score confidence: low. New assessment, source 43.

The widest thematic match, but the weakest recommendation of these four. Its broad comparison can generate useful questions; the numerical index and long-range forecasts do not merit the trust one would place in a validated causal model.

Veto review: V1 is a close call. Kenneth Pomeranz argues that energy use dominates the preindustrial index, that regional units are problematic, and that measurement does not establish the proposed causal account. He nevertheless finds value in the narrative. Morris's response and methodological appendix openly discuss assumptions, error and ways to challenge the model. My judgment is that this establishes a contested and weakly validated synthesis, but not conclusively that its central geography–technology explanation depends on a material falsehood or invalid inference. The no-veto decision has LOW confidence; disclosure alone would not rescue a demonstrated central failure. V2: no evidence-subordinating allegiance established. V3: comparative mechanisms remain. V4: forecasts are vulnerable, but historical explanation supplies substantial independent value. Retain at a low priority rather than treating its model as settled knowledge. Decision confidence: low.

Edition and identity: First published in 2010. The verified Profile paperback is dated 4 August 2011, ISBN 9781846682087. The first year and purchase-edition year are kept separate.

## Reading order and limits

Start with ASML's Architects for industrial capability, then Never at Rest for scientific practice. X, Y & Z is shorter and makes a useful study of cooperation under secrecy. Why the West Rules—for Now is the lowest-priority work here because the breadth and direct fit exceed the strength of its causal validation. It remains included as an eligible, non-vetoed source book.

For Morris, the methodological appendix is evidence of transparency, not a cure for invalid causation. Sensitivity to score changes also does not by itself validate the selected variables. The V1 decision therefore remains open to revision if stronger evidence establishes that a central conclusion requires an invalid inference. No score was calculated by pretending the disputed claims were correct.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 21:25, Europe/Warsaw. Every current entry has one numerical score: 975 recommended-list entries and 173 vetoed entries. Vetoed scores remain counterfactual. · · · · .

The E/S/D variables above are raw linear assessments, not previously squared contributions. The latest ten positive assessments, rule-11 decisions, exclusions and veto decisions remain unchanged: this is a reassessment of the preference deductions, not a fresh full-text review. Each book links to its prior assessment and contributing source analyses. Raw points and final contributions are stored separately, preventing a second application of the quadratic curve.

The earlier cache-only method missed many accessible counts. The repeatable method is: resolve the exact work and edition ISBN/ASIN; retrieve its public Amazon product page; read `acrCustomerReviewText` and, when present, the `total-review-count` global-rating summary; check title, author, language and count agreement; save the URL, count, timestamp and evidence. Amazon Australia and Italy supplied most newly recovered counts. Other marketplaces and cached Amazon pages supplied further observations. Amazon search and Open Library edition metadata locate alternative editions and verify an absent byline; library rating counts never enter the score.

Use the largest verified observed aggregate for the matching work in English when editions have separate rating pools. This makes the selection explicit and avoids treating a little-used reprint or translation as the whole book. Never add counts across editions or marketplaces. A nominated series requires its own matching set listing; individual-volume counts are not combined. Translations, companions, summaries and different volumes are rejected. Failed access and absent rating controls do not mean zero ratings.

The evidence file records the exact count, page URL, title/author match, retrieval time, relevant count markup, and response hash for direct observations. Earlier Amazon.com counts retain their crawl-age limits and received a separate . These are selected product aggregates, not a claim that Amazon combines every edition worldwide. Counts can change over time; the recorded snapshot determines this review. The , , , and document the method.

E through P are the final criterion contributions. Every deduction is shown separately.

The validator checks all 1,148 identities, finite single totals, raw criterion bounds, each contribution and deduction, threshold boundaries, capped publication age, ranking, table coverage, local links, source numbers and unchanged historical files. The 301 hard exclusions remain unscored and separate. Arithmetic and coverage confidence: high. Book-level assessment confidence is recorded individually.

## Hard exclusions and unresolved non-book references

These fiction works were discarded before scoring. They are in neither master book list.

The reference to Ilan Pappé at L1312 names an author, not a particular book; no title was invented. The Aviator at L1136 and The Assassination & Mrs. Paine at L1742 are film/documentary references. The Prashad YouTube suggestion at L186 is not a book. They belong in neither book list. Unspecified “other books” are likewise not resolvable nominations. *At the Café* is retained as philosophical exposition in dialogue form; dialogue alone is not enough to classify a work as fiction.

## Reading priority and limits

The strongest fit is *Bankrupting the Enemy* (88): financial constraints are tied to trade and strategic choice. *How to Hide an Empire* (87) gives a broader account of infrastructure and overseas power. *The Structure of Scientific Revolutions* (86), *Fooled by Randomness* (85) and *Conjectures and Refutations* (85) are strong methodological fits, with some material likely familiar to a theoretical physicist. *The Guns of August* remains at 85 for strategic rigidity and operational failure, not as a complete account of war origins.

At the low end, *I've Been Fired!*, the Goggins books, *The War of Art*, *Reasons to Stay Alive* and *CHAOS* have little direct fit, weakly demonstrated general transfer, or both. Their inclusion is required by the non-veto completeness rule; it does not imply a purchase recommendation. Conversely, high reader enthusiasm does not override the vetoes or repair causal errors.

## Verification record

- 136 nonfiction entries have ten bounded component scores, one permitted thematic deduction, a computed total, a confidence level and a gate decision. - 127 non-veto entries occur in the ranked table and in RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md; nine current-source vetoes occur in VETOED_BOOKS.md. - All 28 earlier score vectors were compared with the relevant earlier reports. Source unions retain every earlier source number. - Every new linked ISBN passes its check-digit test. Format exceptions and uncertain identities are marked. - Fiction is absent from both master book lists. Existing analysis files are preserved as history. - Coverage and live Amazon availability remain limited as stated above; neither is claimed complete.

## Hard exclusions — fiction

These 47 works or series receive no score, no veto and no entry in either master book list. A fictional work does not become eligible because a commenter places it in a nonfiction thread. *The Great Divorce* is an allegorical narrative; *A Raisin in the Sun* is a play. *The Executioner’s Song* is retained as documentary literary nonfiction, with the contested genre boundary and low confidence made explicit in M131.

## Non-book references and unresolved nominations

The films *The Endurance* (2001), *Jaws*, *The Great Escape*, *Peeping Tom* and *Psycho* are not added as book nominations. Neil Postman’s “Social Science as Theology” is an essay reference, not a separately identified source book. Podcast discussion, including the Stephens–Townsend–Murphy Party, does not nominate an additional book. Author-only recommendations are not expanded into bibliographies.

Four apparent joke titles could not be tied to a reliable book record: “Chimney Sweep & Mayor,” “Police & Astronaut,” “Lawyer and Deep Sea Diver,” and “Park Ranger & Uber Driver.” They are unresolved references, not proved nonexistent books, and enter neither master list.

The phrase “Fly like a bird to ur mountain” appears to refer to the Chinese title of *Educated*; a reply also suggests that identity. It is treated as a probable alias, not a separate book. “Brothers (JFK & RFK)” is provisionally identified as David Talbot’s *Brothers*; its veto and counterfactual are conditional on that identification. *Batavia’s Graveyard* is distinct from Peter FitzSimons’s *Batavia*; *What Remains* is distinct from *Strength in What Remains*. The two McCullough descriptions about Panama and the Brooklyn Bridge identify *The Path Between the Seas* and *The Great Bridge*.

Corrected source/catalogue errors include the POW identities in *The Fifteen*; Johanson’s name and the overstatement of a final “missing link” solution in *Lucy*; the first-publication years of *Raising Hare* (2024), *The Culture of Narcissism* (1979), *People of the Blue Water* (1954) and *The Fifties* (1993); and the author order for Philip Norman. Recent 2026 publications were checked against the assessment date and were not discarded solely because older catalogues lacked them.

## Repository reconciliation and verification

Source 4 adds 118 new retained entries and updates 26 existing retained entries with all prior source numbers preserved. It adds 14 new veto records and adds source 4 to the two existing vetoes. The combined veto register therefore has 30 unique entries, one with a conditional identity. The retained and veto lists do not overlap. All 160 vectors have ten bounded criterion values plus exactly one T value, and all totals were recomputed. The 144-row ranked table and master retained entries are generated from the same assessed records. Fiction and non-book references are absent from both lists. Previous analysis files are byte-for-byte preserved. Completeness applies to the extracted candidate set, not to the inaccessible Reddit replies.

The earlier cache-only method missed many accessible counts. The repeatable method is: resolve the exact work and edition ISBN/ASIN; retrieve its public Amazon product page; read `acrCustomerReviewText` and, when present, the `total-review-count` global-rating summary; check title, author, language and count agreement; save the URL, count, timestamp and evidence. Amazon Australia and Italy supplied most newly recovered counts. Other marketplaces and cached Amazon pages supplied further observations. Amazon search and Open Library edition metadata locate alternative editions and verify an absent byline; library rating counts never enter the score.

Use the largest verified observed aggregate for the matching work in English when editions have separate rating pools. This makes the selection explicit and avoids treating a little-used reprint or translation as the whole book. Never add counts across editions or marketplaces. A nominated series requires its own matching set listing; individual-volume counts are not combined. Translations, companions, summaries and different volumes are rejected. Failed access and absent rating controls do not mean zero ratings.

The evidence file records the exact count, page URL, title/author match, retrieval time, relevant count markup, and response hash for direct observations. Earlier Amazon.com counts retain their crawl-age limits and received a separate . These are selected product aggregates, not a claim that Amazon combines every edition worldwide. Counts can change over time; the recorded snapshot determines this review. The , , , and document the method.
